soft.comment: diffuse ambient shadow on light surfaces — rests just above the page

lifted.comment: soft, deeper — hover and floating surfaces on light

soft-deep.comment: dark-surface counterpart of soft — black, since a light shadow does not read on dark

halo.comment: a card's hover on a light surface: a soft halo of ink. IDENTICAL geometry to halo-deep — the two must always be the same size and spread; only the colour differs, because a dark shadow is what reads on light and light is what reads on dark.

halo-deep.comment: a card's hover on a dark surface: a bright, saturated indigo glow with a lit edge. Same geometry as halo — keep them in step.

highlight.comment: the light top edge of a raised surface on dark

effect.$comment: Hover lightness bump (CSS filter: brightness) for themes whose controls change lightness instead of lifting.

lighten-strong.comment: 22% brighter — the bump a theme needs when brightness is carrying the whole hover, with no lift to help. 1.1 reads on a pale fill and all but vanishes on a deep one, which is what left Adventure's pine buttons looking inert.

subtle.comment: outer bound of the hand-placed sticker tilt — components scale this by a per-instance multiplier in -1..1

none.comment: no tilt — cards stay square on hover

still.comment: no transform at all. Distinct from `rest`, an identity translate: an identity transform is still a transform change, which promotes the element to its own layer and can shift its text by a subpixel on hover. A theme that does not move things should use this.

300.comment: one loop of a continuous ambient motion — slow enough to read as texture moving, not as a control reacting

linear.comment: the only correct curve for a seamless loop — any easing makes a continuous animation pulse at the seam
